title.narrative: Strengthened Territorial Management Practices for the Exercise of Collective Rights

description.narrative:
The project seeks to strengthen the organizational and advocacy capacities of women and men for territorial governance and the exercise of collective rights. To this end, it aims to consolidate sustainable territorial management practices for the protection and defense of territories, while fostering strategic alliances and coordination among social organizations to support collective action, social resistance, and mobilization. Ultimately, the project aims to enhance territorial governance through the implementation of concrete practices of resistance and advocacy, building on actions developed in previous phases of the project.
Project beneficiaries are women and men from Indigenous territories and peri-urban areas. Implementation will take place in three river basins: the Maylanco basin, involving the communities of Larati, AULL, and Ucuhi; the Mamoré basin, in coordination with the CONISUR, TIPNIS, and Isiboro sub-central organizations; and the Poopó basin, with the Ayllu San Agustín de Puñaca.
The expected outcome is that women and men participating in the project improve their living conditions through the effective exercise of collective rights.
